piece.title: String Quartet in E-flat major
piece.why: Fanny Hensel's Romanza: Violin I states the theme, the viola echoes a phrase, then the cello restates the theme in its high tenor register under a Violin I countermelody.

roster.label: Quartet that lost its viola: 2 violins, cello, + a clarinet

plan.summary: As written (no arranging): the original parts are handed out unchanged. The source parts in score order (Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Violoncello) are paired with the players sorted from highest to lowest range center (the midpoint of each player's sounding range): Violin 1 → Violin; Violin 2 → Violin; Viola → Clarinet in B♭; Violoncello → Cello. No octave shifts, no chord changes beyond what a one-note instrument requires (a wind or brass player plays the top note of a double stop or chord), and no repair: a note outside a player's range stays where it is and is marked with an x notehead.
